title: MONUSCO Chief James Swan Reaffirms Ituri as 'Strategic Priority' in Bunia Visit
detail: James Swan, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and head of MONUSCO, met Ituri's provincial governor in Bunia on Thursday, Sept 24, 2026, and declared that "Ituri province remains MONUSCO's strategic priority." Swan pointed to ADF violence as continuing to restrict civilian movement, access to basic services and humanitarian operations in the province, alongside the ongoing Ebola outbreak. He said MONUSCO has deployed mobile operational bases and rapid response units and mobilized logistics to support the medical response, including facilitating team mobility and providing security for health facilities.

media.caption: MONUSCO chief James Swan in Bunia, Ituri, reaffirming the mission's support amid security and health crises, Sept 24-25, 2026

confidenceReason: Reported by Radio Okapi (tier 2) directly quoting Swan's on-the-record statement in Bunia; a single-outlet account of a routine diplomatic visit, not independently corroborated elsewhere.

title: Ebola Toll Reaches 3,779 Deaths Among 7,820 Cases as North Kivu Caseload Overtakes Ituri Trend
detail: Africa CDC reported 7,820 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases and 3,779 deaths as of Sept 25, 2026 — a rise of 47 cases and 20 deaths from the Sept 23 count of 7,773 cases and 3,759 deaths — spanning 63 health zones across seven provinces (49 active, 8 in sustained control, 6 in control phase). Regional trends have diverged sharply over the latest three-week period: Ituri, the outbreak's epicenter, saw cases fall 25% and deaths drop 31%, while North Kivu's caseload rose 56% and deaths there climbed 19%, giving North Kivu the highest case-fatality ratio nationally at roughly 60.5%. About 65% of reported cases are still occurring within communities rather than being caught by surveillance, and contact tracing has improved from 10 to 20 contacts per case but remains below the 60-contact target. Response capacity has expanded to 24 laboratories running 3,400+ daily tests, with over 100,000 test kits distributed.

media.caption: Africa CDC's Sept 25, 2026 Ebola outbreak update as the toll reached 7,820 cases and 3,779 deaths, with North Kivu's caseload overtaking Ituri's

confidenceReason: Figures are attributed directly to Africa CDC, a continental public health authority, and are consistent with the trajectory of prior INSP/Ministry of Communication tallies reported through September.
